quick_skim.title: Exponentially Consistent Low Complexity Tests for Statistical Sequence Matching
quick_skim.abstract: Towards practical applications of statistical sequence matching, we propose low complexity tests that are exponentially consistent and bound the exponential decay rates for error probabilities of our proposed tests. In statistical sequence matching, one is given two databases of multiple sequences, where in each database, each sequence is generated i.i.d. from a distinct distribution. A pair of sequences, one from each database, is said matched if they are generated from the same distribution. The number of matched pairs of sequences, a.k.a, the number of matches, can be either zero or positive. We consider both cases of known and unknown number of matches. When the number of matches is known and positive, the task is to identify all matched pairs of sequences. To construct fixed-length tests, we calculate the scoring function values for all pairs of sequences across the two databases and identify the matched pairs as those having small enough pairwise scoring function values. We show that our proposed test is exponentially consistent, which strikes a better tradeoff between complexity and performance than existing fixed-length tests that use exhaustive search. To construct sequential tests, we need an additional positive threshold to determine the stopping time, and we show that our sequential test achieves strictly better performance than our fixed-length test. Subsequently, we generalize our results to the case with unknown number of matches.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: For sequence matching in large databases such as metagenomes, the authors propose exponentially consistent low-complexity tests with bounds on error decay rates. They handle both known and unknown numbers of matches, enabling efficient yet reliable matching between sequence databases.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 在宏基因组等大规模序列比对场景中，需要低复杂度且可靠的统计检验来识别数据库间的匹配序列。本文提出指数一致的低复杂度检验，并推导出错误概率的指数衰减界。该方法适用于已知或未知匹配数的情况，能准确识别所有匹配序列对。这为宏基因组测序数据的序列匹配和比对提供了高效的统计学基础。
